description: A statement that an agent asserts or proposes within a discourse graph. Claims are the primary assertional unit: they can be supported or opposed by evidence, address questions, and be compiled into theories or models. A claim gains evidential weight ONLY from evidence (tech.scios.rrgi.supports/opposes are strictly evidence→claim); a claim built on prior claims records that descent with tech.scios.rrgi.derivedFrom, which carries no evidential weight — so a derived claim is structurally, visibly untested until evidence arrives; two claims that cannot both be true are linked with tech.scios.rrgi.contradicts. The epistemic status distinguishes between claims (believed with adequate evidence), hypotheses (posed for discussion without asserting belief), and community-defined variants. Grounded in the MIRA community schema (github.com/MIRA-science/schema, mira.yaml, Claim class); first ported (2026-05) from the DiscourseGraphs coalition's org.discoursegraphs.claim (github.com/DiscourseGraphs/schemas) — historical lineage, kept as attribution. Dual-addressing of every reference is an RRGI extension intended to be proposed upstream.

text.description: The claim text. A declarative statement that can be supported or opposed by evidence.

epistemicStatus.description: The epistemic status of this statement. Defaults to unspecified (generic statement) per incremental formalization: authors can refine to 'claim', 'hypothesis', etc. as their thinking develops.

description.description: Optional elaboration, context, or reasoning behind this claim.

contextEntities.description: Aboutness: the concrete concepts and entities this claim is about (e.g. phenomena, materials, instruments, datasets, populations, tasks) — the same field evidence and questions carry. Records point at external subject authorities rather than minting an internal entity registry, following Wikidata P921 'main subject' ('primary topic of a work or act of communication') and schema.org 'about' ('The subject matter of an object'); each entry's optional uri resolves to the external authority. Stamped at authoring/decomposition time; enables shared-concept joins across literatures — two claims about one concept under different vocabularies become findable.

name.description: Name or identifier of the concept or entity. Prefer specific over generic — a rare, precise concept is worth more to discovery than a broad one.

uri.description: Optional URI identifying this entity in an external ontology or knowledge base (e.g. a Wikidata item) — the P921/about pattern: reference external authorities, never mint an internal registry.
